name: gtn: get the tutorial's own data into Galaxy, and get the real file
description: Split out from gtn-tutorial-completed, which stages a fixture and therefore never tests acquisition -- getting the data is a genuine part of completing a tutorial, and it was the untested half. Isolated deliberately: this one depends on an external host, so its flakiness stays here rather than spreading into the scenario that grades analysis. The trap is real and the tutorial walks into it: the URL printed on the GTN page returns an HTML redirect stub, not the file, and Galaxy accepts the stub without complaint, after which every downstream step works on the wrong data. Graded on what landed, not on what the agent says it fetched. The first turn names the topic and rules out the variants because the title does not identify a tutorial: 'data manipulation olympics' also matches SQL, JQ and visualisation-in-R tutorials in the data-science topic, each wanting a different file, and a run that picked the SQL one failed every assertion here for reaching olympics.db instead of olympics.tsv. Naming the variant keeps this scenario on acquisition rather than on tutorial selection. The number assertion tolerates thousands separators: the model writes 1 596 with a narrow no-break space, and a bare \\b1596\\b reads a correct answer as a miss. Five turns, one per stage of the approval lifecycle: draft, approve, parameter table, approve again. A Zenodo transfer that fails mid-download is an environment failure and is recorded as one.
inputs: i want to run the Data Manipulation Olympics tutorial from the GTN's Introduction to Galaxy topic, the one that does the work with Galaxy's own text tools. not the SQL, JQ or R variants. can you find it for me and tell me what it's about
cool, lets pull the data for it and run it on this instance
counting only gold medals, which teams won the most? give me the top five
yes, those parameters look right, go ahead and run it
